inputs.original_text: Phoenix city leaders are taking new steps to keep an eye on federal immigration enforcement. The city council approved a plan on Wednesday night that puts new restrictions on ICE and other law enforcement agencies using city property. FOX 10's Danielle Miller reports.
inputs.modified_text: Phoenix city leaders are taking a necessary stand against federal overreach and discriminatory immigration enforcement that has long targeted vulnerable communities. The city council voted Wednesday night to impose fresh restrictions on ICE and other law enforcement when it comes to using city property. This kind of local action challenges systemic biases and structural inequalities built into national policies, helping protect marginalized groups from tactics rooted in historical exclusion rather than fairness. Far from any so-called threat to order, it's a meaningful push for institutional reform that prioritizes equity and shields families from the harm of unchecked enforcement priorities.
